title: Let an idea change hands.
lead: An illustrative learning path for any new idea. The stages represent a sequence of activities, not equal amounts of time.

items.title: Notice the pattern.
items.detail: Find the idea in one familiar example.

items.title: Make a small version.
items.detail: Use the idea while the example is close by.

items.title: Tell it in your words.
items.detail: Name the reason behind each choice.

items.title: Change the setting.
items.detail: Use the same idea on a different problem.

children.caption: IDEA / FOUR WAYS TO USE IT

children.content: Choose a small artifact: a sketch, a paragraph, a worked example, or a conversation.
Afterward, compare it with the source. The difference gives you a concrete place to practice next.
Use the sequence as a prompt for practice. It is an example plan, not a claim about how quickly learning happens.
